title: Colored Jones and the volume conjecture

items.title: Normalized colored Jones sequence
items.statement:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate, put $q=A^4$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}=q_K^{-1}$, and work over $F=\mathbb Q(A)$. An oriented knot in $S^3$ means a smooth embedded circle with an orientation, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. For an integer $r$, put
$$[r]=\frac{q_K^r-q_K^{-r}}{q_K-q_K^{-1}},\qquad [m]!=\prod_{r=1}^{m}[r]\quad(m\ge1),\qquad [0]!=1.$$
For each $N\ge1$, put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$.
For each integer $N\ge1$, let $V_N$ have basis $v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}$ and define the $U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action in the library coproduct convention by
$$K_Lv_j=q_L^{N-1-2j}v_j,\qquad Ev_j=[N-j]v_{j-1},\qquad Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},$$
where $v_{-1}=v_N=0$. In the universal $R$-matrix formula use $q_K$ and $H v_j=(N-1-2j)v_j$; on $V_N\otimes V_N$ its action is the finite sum
$$\mathcal R_N=q_K^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}\,E^r\otimes F^r,$$
and the positive crossing is $c_N=P\mathcal R_N$, where $P(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. This is an irreducible module of dimension $N$. Equip these matrices with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon data: the twist matrix is the scalar $\theta_N=\lambda_N I$ with $\lambda_N=(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}$, and the matrix $G_N=(-1)^{N-1}\operatorname{diag}(A^{2(N-1-2j)})_{j=0}^{N-1}$ is the pivotal comparison used in the closure trace. The resulting generic quantum dimension is
$$d_N=\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A^{2N}-A^{-2N}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$
Use the contragredient left-dual action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ on $V_N^*$, with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(f\otimes v)=f(v)$ and coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v_j\otimes v_j^*$. The ambient category is the $F$-linear category generated by the modules $V_N$ for all $N\ge1$ under finite tensor products, contragredient duals, finite direct sums and images of module-idempotents, whose morphisms are module homomorphisms, and whose tensor-product action is induced by the stated Hopf coproduct; its tensor unit is $F$ with the trivial action, so its tensor-unit endomorphism ring is $F$. These matrix data satisfy the ribbon-category axioms: braiding and inverse braiding, both duality snakes, monoidal pivotal comparison, balancing and dual compatibility of twist. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the framed-tangle and Markov constructions. An oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ presented as the closure of an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ has generic normalized value
$$J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}\in F,$$
where, for a word $\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$ with $\varepsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, $w(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$, and $\rho_N(\beta)$ is obtained by replacing each positive braid generator by $c_N$ on the corresponding adjacent tensor factors and each inverse generator by $c_N^{-1}$, then composing in word order. This quotient is an integral Laurent polynomial in $A^4$. Define the **normalized colored Jones sequence** by the unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ satisfying $J_N(K;A^4)=J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;A^4)$. Its root value $J_N(K;q_N)$ is obtained by substituting into this Laurent polynomial. The variable transport to the ordinary Jones convention is $t=q^{-1}=A^{-4}$.

references.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§5.6, 8.3, 8.9–8.10
Noah Snyder and Peter Tingley, The half-twist for U_q(g) representations, §§3–5
Hitoshi Murakami, An Introduction to the Volume Conjecture, §2.4
Kazuo Habiro, On the quantum sl2 invariants of knots and integral homology spheres, §§2.3 and 3.3

items.title: All generic colored Jones matrices satisfy the ribbon identities

references.title: Noah Snyder and Peter Tingley, The half-twist for U_q(g) representations
Hitoshi Murakami, An Introduction to the Volume Conjecture

items.statement:
Let $A$ be indeterminate, $F=\mathbb Q(A)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. For every integer $N\ge1$, the concrete module, finite $R$ series, duality, pivotal comparison $G_N$, and twist $\lambda_N$ in the normalized colored Jones definition are admissible ribbon data. More precisely, take the $F$-linear category generated by all those modules under finite tensor products, chosen contragredient duals, finite direct sums, and images of module-idempotents, with all module maps as morphisms. Its braiding on weight vectors is the finite series
$$R_{X,Y}=D_{X,Y}\sum_{r\ge0}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}E_X^r\otimes F_Y^r,\qquad D_{X,Y}(x_h\otimes y_k)=A^{hk}x_h\otimes y_k.$$
The sum is finite on each pair. Its pivotal comparison on weight $h$ is $(-1)^h q_K^h$, and its twist on $V_N$ is $(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}I$. These give natural invertible braidings with both hexagons, both duality snakes, the balancing identity and dual compatibility of twist. In particular all colors $N$, rather than a fixed bounded range of colors, are covered.

items.title: The normalized generic colored Jones quotient is an integral Laurent polynomial

references.title: Noah Snyder and Peter Tingley, The half-twist for U_q(g) representations
Hitoshi Murakami, An Introduction to the Volume Conjecture

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every integer $N\ge1$ and every finite braid word $\beta$ on $b\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the normalized generic quotient
$$\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes b}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}$$
belongs to $\mathbb Z[A^4,A^{-4}]$. Consequently there is a unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ whose substitution $q=A^4$ equals that quotient. It is independent of the braid representative, has $J_N(\bigcirc;q)=1$, and agrees with the normalized colored Jones convention of Murakami’s explicit matrix definition in the variable $q$. Its value at every nonzero complex $q$, in particular $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$, means evaluation of this Laurent polynomial; it never means division by the specialized quantum dimension.

items.title: Finite colored Jones evaluation is exact and representative-independent
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the prescribed generic matrix ribbon data for the $N$-dimensional color, where $N\ge1$. For every finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the algorithm performs finitely many exact operations, including exactly one crossing-matrix update per letter and one finite pivotal-trace contraction, and returns the generic normalized value $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(\widehat\beta;q)$. If two such braid words close to the same oriented unframed knot, their returned generic values agree. The unique Laurent representative belongs to $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and its evaluation at any nonzero complex $q$ is defined, including at $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$.

references.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§8.9–8.10
Hitoshi Murakami, An Introduction to the Volume Conjecture, §§2.4–2.5

items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice supplies Markov's theorem and implies countable choice; countable choice is also the exact hypothesis of the framed ribbon-tangle evaluator.

items.title: Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the normalized colored Jones sequence used below.

Let $K$ be an oriented smooth knot in $S^3$, let $E_K$ be its compact exterior, and equip $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ with a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric $g$ having exactly one peripheral torus cusp. Write $\operatorname{Vol}_g(K)$ for its Riemannian volume. Let $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ be the normalized $N$-dimensional colored Jones Laurent polynomial with $J_N(\bigcirc;q)=1$, in the variable $q=A^4$ declared in the generic color definition. Put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$. The conjecture is that $J_N(K;q_N)\ne0$ for all sufficiently large $N$ and that
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|J_N(K;q_N)|=\operatorname{Vol}_g(K).$$
This is the real absolute-value formulation; the complex-volume refinement is a separate conjecture.

items.title: One finite sequence value does not determine asymptotic growth
items.statement: For every positive real sequence $(a_N)_{N\ge1}$, every real $V>0$, and every integer $N_0\ge1$, if $(2\pi/N_0)\log(a_{N_0})=V$, then $\lim_{N\to\infty}(2\pi/N)\log(a_N)=V$.
